User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the EduAI application.

googleId.description: The user's Google ID for authentication.

subscriptionId.description: Reference to Subscription. (Relationship: User 1:1 Subscription). Represents the user's current subscription.

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the user account was created.

Subscription.title: Subscription
Subscription.description: Represents a user's subscription plan and associated limits.

planType.description: The type of subscription plan (e.g., free, premium).

apiQuota.description: The maximum number of API requests allowed per time period.

apiKey.description: API key for accessing the GenAI model.

model.description: The AI model associated with the subscription (e.g., ai 2.5 flash).

paymentMethodId.description: Reference to PaymentMethod. (Relationship: Subscription 1:1 PaymentMethod). Represents the user's chosen payment method.

PaymentMethod.title: PaymentMethod
PaymentMethod.description: Represents a user's payment method for subscriptions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the payment method.

type.description: The type of payment method (e.g., credit card, PayPal).

details.description: Encrypted details of the payment method (e.g., credit card number).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to manage users, their subscriptions, payment methods, and API usage for the EduAI application. The structure prioritizes authorization independence and supports secure list operations.

Users are stored under the `/users/{userId}` path, which facilitates easy user management and clear ownership. Each user document contains a `subscriptionId` which references their current subscription.

Subscriptions are stored in `/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` and include details about the plan type, API quota, API key, model, and a reference to the payment method (`paymentMethodId`).

Payment methods are stored in `/payment_methods/{paymentMethodId}` and are associated with a user ID. They include sensitive details that should be encrypted. This setup allows easy management of payment methods and associating them with users.

To support features like "Topic Brainstormer", "Presentation Outliner", "Analogy Finder", "Research Outline Generator", "Smart Reference Finder", "Academic Paraphraser", and "Summarizer", it is assumed that the API keys in the `Subscription` document are used by a backend service with appropriate security measures to prevent abuse.

This structure enables Authorization Independence by avoiding hierarchical `get()` calls. Security rules can be written based on the `request.auth.uid` and the data present in each document, without needing to fetch parent document data.

QAPs are supported through structural segregation. User data, subscription data, and payment method data are stored in separate collections, each with its own security rules. This prevents unauthorized access and enables secure list operations within each collection.
